clue.text: Not worried about heartless judge

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word for judge is removed

blocks.note: CA, short for circa, means about
a referee judges a match

explanation.surface: Someone relaxed about appearing before a judge who shows no mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' looks like a description of a harsh judge, but it cuts the middle letter out of the official's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree describes a person free of anxiety, a straightforward synonym for untroubled.

clue.text: Gentleman rises after young socialite remains

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman entering society
the title for a gentleman, here running upwards

explanation.surface: A gentleman stands up when a young society girl stays behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the young socialite first; the reversed title follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something broken or destroyed, a plural-sense noun like remains.

clue.text: Staggered seeing safe almost forced

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for safe is dropped

blocks.note: sure in the sense of safe, as in a sure bet
prised open means forced open

explanation.surface: Someone is stunned to find a safe has nearly been broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: To be staggered is to be astonished, which is what surprised means as an adjective.

clue.text: They cut fruit around summer's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter only
around means one piece is wrapped about the other

blocks.note: prunes are dried plums
the final letter of summer

explanation.surface: Orchard work: chopping back fruit trees as summer closes.
explanation.walkthrough: The R from summer goes inside PRUNES, before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pruners are cutting tools or people who trim plants, so they are things that cut.

clue.text: Jelly fish could be its source

definitions.text: Jelly fish could be its source

blocks.note: surface reading: a jellyfish, the sea creature, as the origin of something

blocks.clueFragment: Jelly fish could be its source
blocks.note: setter's reading: a savoury jelly that may be made from fish stock

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Jellyfish' into two words: the jelly is the answer, and fish stock is one of the things it can be set from.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a clear savoury jelly made from meat or fish stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Artist upset over adult model support

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run upwards

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist, here turned round
mature means grown up

explanation.surface: An artist is distressed about a grown-up model needing support.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the reversed artist on top of MATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An armature is the internal framework a sculptor builds to hold up a clay or plaster model.

clue.text: Harmless government's leader in African country

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Benin is a West African country
the first letter of government

explanation.surface: A political observation about the head of an African government being harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means gentle and causing no harm, so it is a synonym of harmless.

clue.text: Naked but for last of lingerie

indicators.note: last of points to the closing letter of the next word

blocks.note: bar as a preposition means except, just like but for
the final letter of lingerie

explanation.surface: Someone would be naked except for a final scrap of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means uncovered or unclothed, a direct synonym of naked.

clue.text: Forward perhaps without a booking

blocks.note: first meaning: frank and open, without reticence; forward is one example
second meaning: not booked in advance, as a seat or table

explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' suggests a football position playing without a yellow card, but it means bold or outspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreserved means both outspoken, showing no restraint, and not set aside by prior booking.

clue.text: Reptile beginning to probe in ground

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: terrain is ground or land
the first letter of probe

explanation.surface: A reptile starts poking around in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, and turtles are reptiles: an example of the class.

clue.text: Type tending to the right?

blocks.note: first meaning: a style of printed lettering
second meaning: slanting rightwards, as such lettering does

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person leaning towards right-wing politics; the question mark warns that both halves belong to printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic names a sloping typeface and also describes the rightward slant of its letters, adjective and noun.

clue.text: Supporter of Queen in old club

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a brassie was an old wooden golf club, roughly a two-wood
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A royal patron of a historic club is described as its supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter of Queen' reads as a royalist, but the definition is just 'Supporter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere, or bra, is an undergarment that supports the breasts; supporter is a playful description.

clue.text: Mars passes circling centre of ellipse

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter
circling means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: runs as in passes or goes
the middle letter of the seven-letter ellipse

explanation.surface: Astronomy: the planet Mars passes along its elliptical orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars is not the planet but the verb to mar, to spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to spoil or damage it, as mars does in the third-person verb form.

clue.text: Outlander power blocking enemy resistance

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so this piece lodges inside another

blocks.note: a foe is an enemy
reign is sovereign power
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A foreign-sounding power meets enemy resistance on its way in.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlander is a person from another country, the old word for an alien or stranger.

clue.text: Passes water by support for tents

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
pees means urinates

explanation.surface: Someone relieves themselves beside the poles holding up a campsite's tents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' sets the support beside the other piece, so it can go first.
explanation.definitionFit: Teepees are conical tents of hide or canvas used by Plains peoples of North America.

clue.text: Properties with power casual about energy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
remiss means careless or negligent
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Property developers being offhand about energy use.
explanation.definitionFit: Premises are buildings with their land, the properties a business occupies.

clue.text: Routine performance taking stage for prize

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: rote is mechanical, routine repetition
a set is the scenery on a stage

explanation.surface: A dancer's routine on stage wins a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rosebud-shaped ribbon badge awarded as a prize at shows and competitions.

clue.text: Metal barrel on good gun

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask
G is the abbreviation for good
the Sten was a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A metal gun barrel fitted on a good weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the barrel sits on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a hard, dense metallic element used in filaments and tools: an example of a metal.

clue.text: African from Lubango landed

indicators.note: from means drawn out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An African traveller has touched down from Lubango.
explanation.walkthrough: Lubango really is a city in Angola, which makes the surface sound factual.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angolan is a person from Angola, a country in southern Africa, so an African.

clue.text: Fools judge endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: to assess is to judge or evaluate

explanation.surface: Fools who keep on judging others forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses is a common insult for stupid people, so a synonym of fools.

clue.text: Southern port having crew cut?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a haven is a harbour

explanation.surface: A sailor in a southern port gets a crew cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a crew cut is a very short haircut, and 'crew' also fits the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaven means closely cut or shaved, as hair is with a crew cut; the definition is a playful example.

clue.text: Convinces Santa to wrap non-stop

indicators.note: the outer words wrap round the result, which sits concealed in them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone persuades Father Christmas to keep wrapping presents without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without pause, a synonym of non-stop.

clue.text: Old face finally wrinkles up

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word
up in a down clue means the letters climb, reading backwards

blocks.note: the last letter of face
lines are wrinkles in the skin

explanation.surface: An elderly face finally creasing into wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: Senile describes the mental decline of old age, so it stands in for old in the sense of aged and failing.

clue.text: Revolting disgust for one previously shunned

indicators.note: revolting here means turning over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to repel is to disgust

explanation.surface: Historic revulsion directed at someone society once avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like a synonym of disgusting, but it signals turning the word over.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper, someone with leprosy, was historically cast out of society, hence an outcast.

clue.text: Practically wild sweetheart making pass

indicators.note: practically means nearly but not quite, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: raving means wild or frenzied
the heart of sweet is its central letter

explanation.surface: A nearly frantic lover makes a romantic advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making pass' suggests flirting, but a pass here is a gap through mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravine is a deep narrow gorge, which can serve as a pass through hills.

clue.text: Found instrument's electronic

blocks.note: an organ is a keyboard instrument
the apostrophe-s read as the contraction of is
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a musical instrument is electronic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find; it is the verb meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something, like a society, is to set it up, which is to organise it.

clue.text: Greek character renounced over decline

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
reneged means went back on a promise

explanation.surface: A Greek figure gives up his principles as his fortunes decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To degenerate is to deteriorate or decline in quality, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Untruths being sly is easy, occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter counts

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that telling untruths comes naturally to the sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lies are deliberately false statements, which is what untruths are.
